openBoundaries.status: Deployed function logic cancels overridden IT execution while billing requires every execution completed. Isolated backend validation/migration review is separate; no production SQL changed. No currently cancelled workflows found in read-only aggregate.

Read-only deployed function inspection indicates that return-for-correction preserves a completed execution, redispatch reuses it, and workflow start requires not_started. Fresh technician correction execution requires separate backend validation and repair; no production SQL changed here.

Existing jobs snapshot exposes identity/type/current visit but omits submitted title, description, priority and site IDs. UI now says the new job was found in current records, not that every submitted field was independently verified.

Live Owner-to-Service diagnosis confirmed that service_departure_readiness_v1 rejects the normal Owner identity with Active Service Tech required before data-maintenance steps. Host-only fix labels and disables the three owner daily-check actions with an accessible Service Tech sign-in required explanation, preserving real Service accounts and owner test personas. Protected legacy RPC call and console warning remain unchanged. Browser tests use actual legacy home functions with synthetic data; production technician accounts and writes were not exercised. The RPC can initialize truck baseline/restock data for valid Service targets and is not a read-only probe.

Some native photo/signature paths are relative storage paths and do not yield usable absolute file links. UI preserves evidence presence instead of inventing a file URL; backend-supported file delivery remains separate.
Existing session survives, but whole parent reload returns embedded Operations to Today. Child reload and Back/Forward preserve workspace.

Owner create to real technician completion/evidence to handoff to review to billing was not mutated in production. Native technician completion remains an AppDeploy workflow, separate from legacy Tech Check records.

Synthetic permanent deletion requires exact typed confirmation and backend receipt plus fresh-list absence. Production dependency guards remain. There is no native undo for permanent deletion; closure preserves history.
